             Preface



            This Book 2 of a series of three books adequately    also those who require a knowledge of Physics
            covers the new NERDC curriculum for Senior           to be able to pursue other courses.
            Secondary School Physics, providing theory,              We are convinced that the books in this
            laboratory work and evaluation exercises,            series satisfy the aims and objectives of the
            including multiple-choice questions in each          new NERDC curriculum for Senior Secondary
            chapter. The series also covers all the topics       Schools and UTME Physics. Accordingly, we
            for the Senior Secondary School Certificate          recommend the books to all students and
            Examinations in all the other West African           teachers of Physics at the Senior Secondary and
            countries, and the UTME examinations.                UTME levels.
            Students are expected to study Books 1 and 2
            in SS 1 and SS 2 respectively, before studying       B.L.N
            Book 3 in SS 3. By so doing, they would have         P.N.O
            covered adequately all the topics listed in the      O.A.L
            Senior Secondary School Physics curriculum.
            This is how the three books should be used so
            as to derive maximum benefit from them. The
            contents of each book in the series are organised
            in a spiral form, moving from the simple topics
            in Book 1 to the more complex topics in Books 2
            and 3. There is no doubt that this approach aids
            learning.
                Since Physics is a practical-oriented
            subject, we have made adequate provision for
            laboratory activities. We advise students and
            teachers to carry out these activities and discuss
            their procedures, observations and inferences.
                Where necessary, we have employed
            Mathematics in order to elucidate purely
            physical concepts. However, we have struck a
            good balance between Mathematics and mere
            description. This is for the benefit of those who
            intend to pursue Physics at higher levels and

             Example 4.2                                                                                         F
             A weightless bar is pivoted at its centre, and
             weights of 10 N and 30 N are attached on one
             side at 4 m and 2 m from pivot. These weights
             are balanced by a weight of 25 N on the other

                                                                Periodic motion
                 The swinging of a simple pendulum will
            be used to illustrate a simple harmonic motion      Cycle
            as performed by a body. In Fig. 5.1, the bob of a   In Fig. 5.1, if the bob of a simple pendulum
            simple pendulum is carefully displaced through      moves from O to A, A to O, O to B, and B to O
            an angle of about 10˚ and then gently released      and this movement is repeated continuously at
            to swing. The pendulum, when displaced,             equal intervals of time, the bob is said to have
            experience a restoring force which causes it to     gone through a cycle. A cycle is, therefore, one
            undergo a regular to and fro motion, past the       complete oscillation made by the bob.
            equilibrium position. O.
                 The force on the pendulum bob and its
            acceleration at equilibrium position O are
            zero. At O, the velocity and the kinetic energy
            are both at their maximum values. At A or B,
            the velocity, and therefore the kinetic energy,
            has become zero. The kinetic energy has been
            converted to potential energy, which is at its
            maximum value at point A or B. The regular
            motion is called an oscillation, or a vibration,
            or a periodic motion and acts about a mean
            position, O, with a continual interchange of
            potential and kinetic energy.                                  A                     B

            Humidity, Relative humidity

            Procedure: Find the approximate focal length,
            f, of the concave mirror provided by focusing
            the image of a distant object on a screen.
            Set up an illuminated object at a distance of
            about 4f from the mirror. Place the screen in a
            position to receive the sharply focused image.
            The mirror will need to be tilted very slightly
            to bring the image on the screen. Measure the
            object distance, u, and image distance, v. (See
            Fig. 13.40.) Interchange the image and the object
            positions and hence obtain a second reading.
            Repeat for values of u of about 3f, 2f and 1 1 f.

            Diverging lens
            The lens does not bring rays parallel to the
            axis to a point focus. The rays are diverged as
            if they were coming from one point behind the
            lens. This point is called a virtual focus and its           Fig. 14.21        Combined converging and
            distance from the optical center of the lens gives                             diverging Lens
            the focal length. Since the diverging lenses
            diverge rays instead of converging them, they
            are said to have a negative power. A combined
            converging lens and diverging lens of equal
            focal lengths behave like a piece of plane glass.
            In Fig. 14.21, a diverging lens diverge parallel
            light rays as if such rays originated from a
            point. This is so because the extent to which
            the diverging lens diverges the rays of light
            is equal to the extent to which the converging               Fig. 14.22        Action of converging and
            lens converges the same rays of light. The effect                              diverging lenses
            they (i.e the combination) have on the incident
            light rays is therefore cancelled out. Thus, the
            parallel light rays incident on the combination
            pass through undeviated.
